key_insight: Thermal scanning probe direct writing enables deterministic, site-selective synthesis of individual perovskite quantum dots with atomic-scale control for quantum light emission.
engineering_relevance: This approach solves a major integration bottleneck for photonic quantum devices by placing high-purity single-photon emitters precisely where cavities and other photonic structures need them.
method: Create a nanoscale-confined formation volume using a thermal scanning probe.
Direct-write CsPbI3 quantum dots with < 25 nm placement control and spectral tunability.
Integrate written emitters with photonic cavities for on-demand coupling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, up to 98% single-photon purity at room temperature, and enhanced spontaneous emission when coupled to cavities.
watch_item: Deterministic writing must still be validated for long-term material stability, reproducibility across large areas, and compatibility with scalable device fabrication.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
